subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub publish a standalone acceptability rule for agent-directed documentation now, and should declared capabilities make an instruction permissible or only reduce it to human review?
rationale: This is a trust-boundary and moderation-policy choice: source inspection cannot safely choose the acceptable scope, enforcement posture, or appeal path without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Publish a narrow standalone policy
options.body: Define task-scoped guidance as allowed and require review or disallow undeclared fetch-and-execute, privilege escalation, confirmation bypass, and out-of-purpose instructions; coordinate manifest references as advisory.

options.title: Fold it into the broader content policy
options.body: Keep this issue as input to the broader content-policy RFC and publish one consolidated public policy after its category and enforcement structure is agreed.

options.title: Defer pending capability-manifest direction
options.body: Wait to publish a rule until the capability-manifest RFC establishes what declarations can reliably support review decisions.

recommendation.title: Publish a narrow standalone policy
recommendation.body: Define task-scoped guidance as allowed and require review or disallow undeclared fetch-and-execute, privilege escalation, confirmation bypass, and out-of-purpose instructions; coordinate manifest references as advisory.

likelyOwner.reason: The related open content-policy RFC is the closest active maintainer-linked forum for deciding the public-policy boundary.
